Reviewed evidence summaries: Air pollution guidance: WHO provides evidence-based air-quality guideline levels for several pollutants, including PM2.5 and PM10; those guidelines are not a personal diagnosis. US AQI: US AQI identifies 101–150 as unhealthy for sensitive groups and 151–200 as unhealthy. Always identify the scale, and do not apply these labels to another country's index. India AQI: India's national AQI has its own index categories and pollutant breakpoints. Do not relabel a US AQI value as Indian AQI. Modelled air-quality forecast: Open-Meteo offers modelled hourly air-quality forecasts. Forecasts can change, and need location, time, AQI scale and attribution. Do not treat them as measured station values. Modelled weather forecast: Open-Meteo provides weather forecast data for a requested location and time. If a forecast is missing, say so rather than predicting a value. Indoor smoke particles: Room air cleaners and compatible building filters can reduce indoor smoke particles. A particle filter does not necessarily remove all gases; consider ventilation and indoor heat as well. Indoor air during pollution events: Outdoor particles can enter buildings; ventilation, indoor sources and temperature also influence indoor conditions. Avoid blanket advice that creates another indoor hazard.
